events.title: Romulus Augustus Proclaimed Roman Emperor
events.description: The general Orestes proclaimed his young son Romulus Augustus emperor of the Western Roman Empire. The boy was a teenager and held little real power.
events.significance: Romulus became the last Western Roman emperor. He was deposed the following year, an event often used to mark the end of the Western Roman Empire.

events.title: Martin Luther Posts the Ninety-Five Theses
events.description: According to tradition, the German monk and theologian Martin Luther posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg. The theses criticized the Church's sale of indulgences.
events.significance: The act is widely seen as the start of the Protestant Reformation, which reshaped Christianity and European politics.

events.title: The Charge at Beersheba
events.description: During World War I, Australian Light Horse troops charged Ottoman defenses at Beersheba in Palestine. The charge captured the town and its vital water wells.
events.significance: It is remembered as one of the last successful cavalry charges in history. It also opened the way for the British advance into Palestine.

events.title: Mussolini Becomes Prime Minister of Italy
events.description: Benito Mussolini took office as Italy's prime minister, at 39 the youngest in the country's history. He was appointed after the Fascists' March on Rome.
events.significance: His appointment began more than two decades of Fascist rule in Italy, and the regime became a model for dictatorships elsewhere in Europe.

events.title: Stalin's Body Removed from Lenin's Tomb
events.description: During the Soviet Union's de-Stalinization campaign, Joseph Stalin's embalmed body was removed from the mausoleum on Red Square. It was reburied nearby beside the Kremlin wall.
events.significance: The move symbolized the Soviet leadership's public break with Stalin's cult of personality after his crimes were denounced.
